meetings.headline: Cable committee began Comcast license-renewal review, dividing up outreach tasks ahead of hiring counsel
meetings.summary: The Cable Advisory Committee began its work on the Comcast license renewal, reviewing a nine-point ascertainment checklist required before a February 2027 deadline and dividing tasks -- facility tours, outreach to town departments, the library and schools, review of the current license, and research into comparable towns' recent cable contracts. No legal contract had yet been reviewed by the town manager, so the committee deferred the public hearing and survey, tentatively targeting an October meeting once counsel is retained.

budget_items.topic: Attorney contract for cable license renewal
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager told a member she has the proposed contract from the attorney but has not had time to review it yet, so no action was needed at this meeting.

budget_items.topic: PEG/local access fee on cable bills
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the public access committee gets a share of subscriber bills as a line item added by Comcast, and wondered how much impact that has and how billing works.
A member said there is a current side letter giving senior citizens a small discount, raised as possible leverage for services like Wi-Fi in the next agreement.
A member said the public access committee is beginning to look at what equipment it has and what it would need to purchase going forward.

decisions.decision: The ascertainment process for the Comcast license renewal must be completed by February 28, 2027.
Brian V will tour the cable operator's technical facilities and the PEG access studio.
A member will research what other communities' cable agreements include, using outreach calls and AI tools as a starting point.
Karen will lead outreach to town departments; the chair will handle the library; Tom will handle the school district.
Tom will contact the school district through the superintendent first, then the IT staff.
Karen will check with the town whether Comcast complaint records exist, including checking the town manager's and select board's offices.
A member will try to find a map of the Comcast service area, checking with the state or Comcast.
Brian L, though absent, will be asked to review the license and other circulated documents.
The public hearing and municipal-wide survey will be held off until more preliminary information is gathered from town departments.
The committee tentatively targeted Tuesday, October 13 or Tuesday, October 20 for its next meeting, pending the attorney; minutes will list the date as 'October Tuesday TBA.'
Brian V, as secretary, will send approved minutes as a PDF to the town clerk going forward.
The chair will hold off on drafting the next agenda until there is word on the attorney/legal contract.

The town manager has a draft attorney contract for the renewal but had not yet reviewed it as of this meeting.

Residents will eventually be asked to weigh in through a public hearing and a survey, but neither has a date yet.
No money or contract terms have been decided; this stage is fact-finding ahead of hiring counsel.

meetings.headline: Cable committee splits tasks and starts hiring a lawyer for the 10-year Comcast franchise renewal
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Cable Advisory Committee, newly reorganized with a chair, vice chair and secretary, held its first substantive meeting on beginning the 10-year renewal of the Comcast cable franchise agreement. Members split into task areas -- hiring a lawyer (paid from PAC/cable funds), liaising with PAC, contacting town and school IT, and public outreach/survey -- and set a virtual meeting for August 13 to review the old contract and the lawyer-hiring process; the meeting closed with a roll-call vote to adjourn.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the cable franchise-renewal lawyer is paid out of PAC (cable) funds, not the town's general funds, and asked whether a select board recommendation or procurement process is needed.

budget_items.topic: Franchise/PEG fee percentage of Comcast revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said PAC currently gets a percentage of Comcast revenue and that this is likely the main negotiation point; another said that percentage is set by state law as a ceiling.
Members discussed whether Comcast provides free internet connections to the town and schools, concluding the town and the school each pay for their own internet.

decisions.decision: Steve Archinbolt was nominated chair, a member was nominated vice chair, and 'the other Brian' (not Brian Leighton) was nominated secretary, before the recorded portion began.
The five committee members agreed to split tasks: hiring a lawyer, liaising with PAC, contacting the town IT/town manager, contacting school IT via the superintendent, and organizing a public survey.
Task assignments were confirmed: Steve to pursue the lawyer process; Joe/Steve Walker/Steve to liaise with PAC; Tom to contact town IT and school IT with a copy of the current cable agreement.
Next meeting set for Thursday, August 13, virtual (Zoom), 6:00 pm, with an agenda of reviewing the old contract and the lawyer-hiring process.
Brian (secretary) agreed to draft minutes and email them to members for approval before submission.

what_happened.line: The newly reorganized committee split its five members into task areas ahead of negotiating a new 10-year Comcast cable franchise agreement.
A member said the negotiation's lawyer would be paid from PAC/cable funds rather than town general funds, and asked whether the select board must approve the hiring process.
Members discussed the percentage of Comcast revenue the cable fund receives as likely the main point of negotiation, noting state law sets a ceiling on that percentage.
The committee set its next meeting for August 13, a virtual session to review the current contract and the lawyer-hiring process.
The meeting closed with a roll-call vote to adjourn; no other votes were taken.

why_it_matters: This negotiation will shape the town's next 10-year cable franchise agreement with Comcast, which funds local public-access programming through the PAC/cable fund rather than general tax dollars.
The revenue-share percentage the committee plans to negotiate is capped by state law and is described as the central lever affecting how much money supports local access TV.
The committee plans a public survey as part of its outreach, so residents may be asked for input before terms are finalized.
